blindSummary: Same-sex activity is legal in this country (one of the few in its region never to criminalise it); there is no legal gender recognition and no protections; chronic instability (coups) and a weak state prevail; social hostility is documented, but without the mass mob-violence pattern seen in one regional peer state.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: only an international legal-aid trust's homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no country-specific page); the trust maps jurisdictions criminalising LGBT people. On its data this country does not criminalise same-sex conduct but has no protections.

A foreign government's 2012 human-rights report on this country: documents the 2012 coup, arbitrary killings, torture, drug-trafficking-linked corruption and impunity - general context; no criminalisation of same-sex conduct.
A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: documents security-force torture, FGM and impunity - general context; the LGBT section notes no criminalisation but societal stigma.

Explainer-site summary of LGBT rights in this country: legal since 1993 (the new penal code that year omits same-sex offences); signed the 2008 UN statement on sexual orientation; only heterosexual married couples are entitled to larger government housing; the 2014 domestic-violence law protects victims regardless of sexual orientation.
Wiki-derived overview site: brief overview of LGBT rights in this country, noting legal challenges and sections on same-sex activity, relationships, adoption and living conditions.

LGBT travel-mapping site country guide: legal since 1993; no partnership recognition; limited protection via the domestic-violence law; no trans framework; a traveller-safety score of 34/100 ('caution'); 9% consider homosexual behaviour morally acceptable - unusually moderate for the region; no visible LGBT scene; some violence cases reported (2018).
